chapter: The brothers and the family's gifts
title: Jazz at Lincoln Center as his father's idea
summary: He sees Jazz at Lincoln Center as Wynton building the hall and codifying the music his father always talked about.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Dad always talked about, “Jazz is a music that must be codified.” It’s the exact opposite of most jazz critics. Jazz critics are, “We need to move forward. The past has already happened. We got to move forward.” But he’s like, “We need to go back and look at this stuff and flesh it out, have this music codified.” That’s what Wynton’s trying to do with Jazz at Lincoln Center.
That’s really – when I think of it now, that’s what I see Jazz at Lincoln Center as.
